title: Quick deep-dive: long-context tricks & eval takeaways
content:
TL;DR:
Quick personal notes from skimming papers and demo talks on long-context handling, cheap compression tricks, and small evals I want to run. Not a polished summary — mostly reminders and experiment ideas for the next sprint.

What I skimmed this week (notes to self):
- "Attention with context-sorted sparsity" (workshop slide dump) — idea: reorder tokens by recentness window then apply structured sparsity. Good for batched steady-state throughput, unclear effect on coherence at boundaries.
- "Lightweight KV compression: quantized deltas" (preprint) — compress KV with deltas between adjacent keys, run-length-like on low entropy spans. Promises 3-4x space reduction for dialogues with repetitiveness.
- Redis-based prefix cache demo (internal prototype) — showed ~12% latency drop p50 after enabling prefix hits for warm sessions; tail impact minimal because most tails were cold (startup cost dominates).

Key takeaways and quick opinions:
- Caching still beats fancy kernel tricks for customer workloads where sessions have repeats (chat apps, copilots). Cache hit-rate is the governing metric.
- Compression of KV is promising but CPU overhead matters: decompression at generation time must be < ~500us/token to be worth the memory savings on A100-style machines.
- Sparse attention variants help inference memory but make batching harder. If we deploy a sparse variant, we need routing to choose between dense/sparse models per-request. That ties into rollout policies.

Immediate experiments to run (prioritized):
1) Tiny KV delta compression prototype against our sample convo dataset (10k sessions):
   - baseline: raw 16-bit keys (current prod-ish format)
   - variant A: per-head linear delta quantization (4-bit) + rle on repeats
   - measure: cache size reduction, decompress CPU us/token on p50/p95 prompt lengths, end-to-end tokens/sec on 1 GPU replica
   - success: >=2.5x reduction and decompress <=400us/token on test hardware

2) Prefix-hit eviction policy ablation (dev cluster):
   - test LRU vs segmented-LRU (session-aware) vs TTL-based
   - metric: effective hit-rate per user, p50 latency delta, and memory churn (evictions/sec)
   - note: instrument to link evictions to real user session ids for debugging

3) Small eval: coherence at context boundary with sparsity
   - generate synthetic sequences where the important entity appears near boundary + repeat after 2k tokens
   - compare dense vs sparse-attn model variants on next-token accuracy over boundary region
   - instrumentation: store attention density maps (coarse) and cross-entropy gap

Open questions (research + infra):
- How brittle are delta-compressed keys to quantization noise when we do KV-propagation across layers? Empirically: does small key-noise change attention argmaxes drastically for tasks with many similar tokens?
- If we use prefix caches across models (e.g., decoder-only v1 -> v2), do we need transformation functions when model embedding spaces shift? A quick approach: keep a tiny remix MLP that maps v1 keys -> v2 key-space. Is that stable/cheap?
- For private deployments: KMS and compression interplay — what metadata do we need to keep to avoid leaking reconstructability (esp. with deterministic compression)?

Notes to self / heuristics for engineering discussions:
- Always compare compression gains vs the increase in CPU latency *and* memory fragmentation risk. A win in bytes doesn't automatically translate to better p99s.
- Use sampled real-user sessions as the canonical dataset for these decisions. Synthetic tends to overstate repetition.
- When proposing rollout: default to a canary that routes 1% of sessions with high-repeat heuristics (session_length>50 and repeat_token_ratio>0.07).

Draft talking points for sync with infra-next-week:
- "We have a 3-pronged short plan: (1) KV delta compression prototype, (2) cache eviction policy experiments, (3) sparsity-boundary evals. Goal: pick 1 for a 6-week intern project and 1 for Q2 spike."
- Cost/risk note: compression increases CPU load; we should quantify GPU-memory vs instance-hour tradeoffs. Quick metric to prepare: GB saved / added CPU-ms per token.

Rough instrument list (what I need on metrics and traces):
- cache.hit_rate by session_id and model_variant
- decode.cpu_us_per_token broken out by: kv_lookup, decompress, lm_forward, kern_launch
- eviction.events with cause tags (ttl/size/lru/seg)
- rollout.bucket -> model_variant mapping with sticky session id

Quick links & refs I want to re-read: (copy-paste for later)
- https://arxiv.org/abs/XXXX.YYYY (delta kv paper)
- internal slide: confluence:long-context-strategy-2029 (section 3, pages on caching)
- github:redwood/kv-cache-experiments/pull/273 — prototype code (watch the decompress path)
- jira:MLOPT-889 — spike ticket for prefix eviction

TODO (short actionable list):
- [ ] Spin up 1-shot delta compression prototype in a docker image (deadline: 2031-02-21)
- [ ] Add metrics hooks for decompress.cpu_us to the decode path (deadline: 2031-02-20)
- [ ] Draft canary rollout doc for the caching model variant (outline by 2031-02-18)

Random heuristics I keep forgetting:
- For dialogue: repeat_token_ratio (unique_tokens / total_tokens) is a much better predictor of cache usefulness than session length alone.
- TTL slightly beats pure LRU in our demo because many sessions are ephemeral (starts with Q/A then ends).

Questions for Aria (ask on sync):
- Did the Redis demo include workload churn patterns? I need the dataset used (small sample).
- Are there existing ops knobs to throttle decompress CPU if we hit host-level contention?

Final micro-plan (next week):
- Monday: implement metric hook for decompress cpu_us; quick smoke test on dev with 20 sessions
- Tue-Wed: baseline run on 10k sessions to collect baseline numbers
- Thu: prototype delta compression and measure the two main numbers (size reduction and cpu_us/token)
- Friday: quick write-up for infra sync, propose intern scope

Notes end — half-structured scratchpad. Will convert to a more formal memo if experiments show wins.

"Be pragmatic: memory wins are only wins if they lower $/token or unlock a cheaper instance tier."
